books.title: L'Empereur-Dieu de Dune (Dune, #4)
books.review: Quite disappointed with the turn of this book. I had a lot of hope for the temporal ellipse but finally, it takes a lot of time to develop for not much. It is above all a philosophy novel at the expense of all the action and rhythm of previous books (which seemed more boring to me than the dune messiah, I was looking forward to finishing it!)

books.title: Harry Potter et l'Enfant Maudit
books.review: Suite of the Saga Harry Potter but not in novel but as a play. This main change makes the plot rather fast, maybe too fast, in a few chapters we spend several script years which can be confusing. Even if I cling to the story but still big points of inconsistency for me who doesn't pass for me, be it on characters or even central points of history. It's not the best work of the Potterverse, but it deserves to exist, I guess, I didn't have a bad time either.

all_reviews.title: Les Enfants de Dune (Dune, #3)
all_reviews.review: We're really getting to the "little common" part of the saga. The weak point I would say is the build-up that really takes its time (350/400 pages) but the pay-off is really satisfying, the end is excellent with exciting adventures and revelations. I see where the wise is going, and I can't wait for the good!

all_reviews.title: Coraline
all_reviews.review: Source story of the eponymous film about a little girl named Coraline. The book follows almost all the elements of the film with some minimal differences. Very good story with a moral about courage. I recommend it for young and old because it reads very well.

all_reviews.title: Le Messie de Dune (Dune, #2)
all_reviews.review: Hard to understand Paul's entire plan and what is going on but I would say that in addition to the chapters of description, the chapters of "action" are really sympathetic with unexpected revelations.

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter et les Reliques de la Mort (Harry Potter, #7)
all_reviews.review: Masterful conclusion for these seven years in this world of witches and witches. True emotions during this reading that seemed so short to me, which demonstrates the quality of J.K Rowling's plumme. The final quest that seems impossible at first makes us travel one last time in this universe that became cult for any reader.

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter et le Prince de Sang-Mêlé (Harry Potter, #6)
all_reviews.review: Wow, what a book! I really like the rhythm: on one side life at school, and on the other side all the revelations that take place in parallel. However, I find the end a little too abrupt to my taste, because some things may seem to be shipped too quickly, even if it was surely the desired effect. We enter definitively into a more adult register, whether by the topics addressed or by the structure of the chapters.

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter et l'Ordre du Phénix
all_reviews.review: Still as well, unlike the film, we understand the order of the phoenix. Book quite massive but the end greatly accelerates the saga.

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter et la Coupe de Feu (Harry Potter, #4)
all_reviews.review: Incredible book and very rich! When we compare the book to the film, I understand the bad feelings that may exist, a lot of details and intrigues went under the carpet which makes the book even more captivating. Relationships are more developed and you really feel the essence of the characters (Overall Hermione!). All the arch of the tournaments allows to raise the lore and stakes and usually come the climax is very nice. Of course I recommend!

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter et le Prisonnier d'Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
all_reviews.review: 3rd opus of the Harry Potter saga, so far the best book of the 3! We're starting to get more serious about the topics and the pace is always as good. Some of the shadow areas of the film are explained, which also makes reading pleasant. In my opinion the characters are the highlight of the book, especially in the various interactions / scene. We only have one hurry: discover the rest!

all_reviews.title: Dune (Dune, #1)
all_reviews.review: There we discover the history of the atreïde lineage of a large house in a science fiction universe far into the future in which they are trapped in a plot that will forever change the face of the universe. The book can be hard enough to read with some rather long passages but the key scenes are nuggeted and you can't stop. The story of the book takes a completely different turn than the film: hawat the mantat is very present he plays in 2 camps despite him, there is also a Paul who becomes aware of his power and that it involves losing his relatives with the Jihad, we switch from brothers of arms to fanatics. Paul's psychology is increasingly being seen and how he fears his power and how he intends to use it. Jessica is less calculator than in the movies but still seems to have a plan in mind. We also discover Anya Paul's sister who was born quite quickly in the book unlike the film. Some parts are more explicit and the temporality is different compared to the film. We discover this very epic SF universe and look forward to finding out what is Paul's continuation and his plans.

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter et la chambre des secrets (Harry Potter, #2)
all_reviews.review: We follow a new year of Harry and his friends in the fantastic magic school: Poudlard. This time, an entire mystery is hovering on the chamber of secrets and an entire investigation is taking place. The book always follows the same pattern as the film, but it is always a pleasure to read it. The build-up of the book works very well and its payoff also, the end is read very quickly! With this part you learn a little more about the global lore of history and that's what you want. The characters are very endearing and you can't wait to read more!

all_reviews.title: Harry Potter à l'école des sorciers (Harry Potter, #1)
all_reviews.review: The book is very nice to read and allows you to discover an incredible world of sorcerer. We follow Harry's adventures and his friends in a mystery that seems bigger than expected.... The book does not diverge too much from the film except for a precise trip, makes us want to read more.
